BiblicalUsage: Trouble and anguish make the wicked afraid, the psalmist asks God to bring him out of the distresses of his enlarged heart, Zephaniah calls the day of the Lord a day of trouble and distress, and the wandering people cried to the Lord in their trouble and He delivered them. The word is the narrow strait where pressure closes in from every side.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Psalm 107:6 is the pattern for every trouble in this word: they cried to the Lord in their trouble, and He delivered them out of their distresses. That is the pattern for every trouble: cry to the Lord, and He delivers.
